target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The default transport budget remains 120 seconds, while macOS WebChat overrides it to five minutes and waits for completion through the existing Gateway `agent.wait` surface before refreshing history. The change does not alter gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

## Evidence

- Current-head freshness: PR head `c54a17b39c8314b0788797dff114928ac57dd492`.
- Current-head packaged macOS app metadata:
  ```text
  OpenClawGitCommit=c54a17b39c
  OpenClawBuildTimestamp=2026-07-07T07:10:56Z
  ```
- Current-head packaged-app proof steps after this patch:
  ```bash
  SKIP_PNPM_INSTALL=1 SKIP_TSC=1 SKIP_UI_BUILD=1 BUILD_ARCHS="$(uname -m)" \
    ALLOW_ADHOC_SIGNING=1 SIGN_IDENTITY="-" ./scripts/package-mac-app.sh

  node openclaw.mjs --dev gateway
  OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=19001 dist/OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw --chat --attach-only
  ```
- Real macOS app entry point used for the proof: the packaged app's status-menu `Open Chat` item opened the native Chat window. The visible native window reported `Gateway connected`, `张贵萍的Mac mini`, and `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark · $0.00`.
- Slow prompt sent through the real native `OpenClaw Chat` input box, not through `gateway call chat.send`:
  ```text
  Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.
  ```
- Current-head real packaged macOS WebChat proof from the native accessibility tree:
  ```text
  PROOF after real UI send on PR head c54a17b39c8314b0788797dff114928ac57dd492:
  AXStaticText name='Gateway connected' value='Gateway connected'
  AXStaticText name='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.' value='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.'
  AXStaticText name='Writing' value='Writing'

  PROOF after 32 seconds on the same current-head native Chat window:
  AXStaticText name='Gateway connected' value='Gateway connected'
  AXStaticText name='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.' value='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.'
  AXStaticText name='Writing' value='Writing'

  PROOF after completion on the same current-head native Chat window:
  AXStaticText name='Gateway connected' value='Gateway connected'
  AXStaticText name='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.' value='Please run this exact terminal command using the terminal and do not reply until it finishes: sleep 45; echo OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE. After it finishes, reply exactly OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE.'
  AXStaticText name='OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE' value='OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE'
  ```
- Observed result after fix on current head: the packaged macOS WebChat app stayed in the visible `Writing` pending state more than 32 seconds after a real UI send, did not show a timeout, and later displayed `OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE` with the pending indicator gone.
- What was not tested: no video recording; the proof above is terminal/app metadata plus native macOS accessibility text copied from the real packaged macOS app window.
- Regression tests rerun on current head:
  ```text
  swift test --filter 'OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`agent wait sends run id and timeout`()|OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`mac chat transport exposes first-run sized pending timeout`()|OpenClawIPCTests.GatewayConnectionControlTests/`mac chat transport opts into first-run sized agent timeout`()'
  ✔ Test "agent wait sends run id and timeout" passed after 0.033 seconds.
  ✔ Test "mac chat transport exposes first-run sized pending timeout" passed after 0.001 seconds.
  ✔ Test "mac chat transport opts into first-run sized agent timeout" passed after 0.001 seconds.
  ✔ Test run with 3 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.035 seconds.

  swift test --filter 'completion wait uses transport opted in timeout'
  ✔ Test "completion wait uses transport opted in timeout" passed after 0.028 seconds.
  ✔ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed after 0.028 seconds.
  ```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Swift unit tests plus macOS terminal behavior proof.
- Target test files: `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift`, `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Scenario locked in: macOS WebChat sends `timeoutMs == 300_000`, completion waits use the transport-scoped budget, pending runs survive past 30 seconds, and pending state clears after completion.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests cover the two changed seams directly: macOS transport timeout selection and shared chat pending/completion state.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the macOS WebChat send path used one short timeout value for both request/ACK delivery and the assistant run budget, so a slow first reply could look timed out or stuck even while the gateway run was still active.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage proving macOS WebChat opts into a first-run-sized assistant budget while preserving the shorter shared/default request timeout.
